submissions.findingTextShort: SURMOUNT-4 found substantial weight regain after tirzepatide withdrawal, while continued treatment maintained and augmented initial weight reduction.
submissions.findingTextNormalized: In SURMOUNT-4, adults without diabetes completed a 36-week tirzepatide lead-in and were randomized to continued maximum-tolerated tirzepatide or placebo for 52 weeks. Continued treatment produced additional mean weight reduction while withdrawal produced substantial regain. This supports a chronic-treatment/maintenance boundary and must not be converted into a guarantee that every patient regains weight or an individualized duration instruction.
submissions.populationContext: Adults with obesity or overweight and a weight-related complication, without diabetes.
submissions.usageContext: Randomized withdrawal maintenance evidence; not individualized prescribing advice.
submissions.uncertaintyNote: Enriched randomized-withdrawal design selects people who tolerated and remained on tirzepatide during lead-in; generalizability to all initiators is limited.

submissions.findingTextShort: A 160-person SURMOUNT-1 DXA substudy found both fat-mass and lean-mass loss during tirzepatide-associated weight reduction.
submissions.findingTextNormalized: In the SURMOUNT-1 DXA substudy, pooled tirzepatide participants had larger reductions in fat mass and lean mass than placebo at 72 weeks. The finding prevents total weight loss from being represented as fat-only loss and does not establish muscle-function loss, sarcopenia incidence, or a universal lean-mass fraction for all users.
submissions.populationContext: 160-participant DXA substudy of adults with obesity or overweight from SURMOUNT-1.
submissions.uncertaintyNote: Substudy size and selection limit precision and transferability; lean mass measured by DXA is not synonymous with skeletal-muscle function.

submissions.findingTextShort: Three-year SURMOUNT-1 data in participants with obesity and prediabetes found sustained weight reduction and substantially less progression to type 2 diabetes with tirzepatide than placebo.
submissions.findingTextNormalized: The 176-week SURMOUNT-1 analysis in participants with obesity and prediabetes found sustained weight reduction and markedly lower progression to type 2 diabetes during treatment with tirzepatide versus placebo. This is a population- and treatment-duration-specific prevention signal and must not be generalized to people without prediabetes, represented as permanent prevention after discontinuation, or substituted for an approved-indication statement.
submissions.populationContext: Adults with obesity and prediabetes in the SURMOUNT-1 three-year analysis.
submissions.usageContext: Long-duration randomized trial evidence; not individualized prevention advice.
submissions.uncertaintyNote: The analysis includes a 17-week off-treatment period and should not be interpreted as proving durable lifetime prevention after treatment cessation.

submissions.findingTextShort: A 12-RCT meta-analysis found increased gallbladder/biliary disease and cholelithiasis risk with tirzepatide, without a clear dose-response pattern.
submissions.findingTextNormalized: A meta-analysis of 12 randomized trials involving 12,351 participants found higher pooled relative risk for gallbladder/biliary disease and cholelithiasis with tirzepatide, while dose subgrouping did not establish a monotonic dose-response. This supports a biliary safety signal but does not provide an individualized absolute risk or prove causality for every biliary event.
submissions.populationContext: Randomized trials in adults with type 2 diabetes or obesity.
submissions.usageContext: Pooled safety signal; current product labeling remains authoritative for clinical warning language.
submissions.uncertaintyNote: Rare-event estimates and comparator mix limit precision; post-marketing surveillance remains relevant.

submissions.findingTextShort: A 17-RCT meta-analysis found no statistically significant pancreatitis-risk difference versus placebo across tirzepatide doses, but confidence intervals were wide.
submissions.findingTextNormalized: Across 17 randomized trials with 14,645 participants and 12-72 weeks of follow-up, adjudication-confirmed pancreatitis risk was not statistically different between tirzepatide doses and placebo, while estimates were imprecise with wide confidence intervals. This is a null counterweight, not proof that pancreatitis cannot occur or justification to remove current label-based pancreatitis precautions.
submissions.populationContext: Randomized tirzepatide trials with placebo or active comparators; pancreatitis analysis versus placebo.
submissions.usageContext: Safety uncertainty/null evidence; regulatory labeling remains authoritative.
submissions.uncertaintyNote: Rare events and limited trial duration reduce power to exclude clinically meaningful uncommon risk.
